correctness.rationale: The Neumann Green kernel produces the exact positive baseline endpoint densities U,V and the homogeneous flux solution p=p_N+J h has endpoint difference zδ and stationary current J=−κzδ, with z=(1+bκ)^{-1}. The interface entropy is (2|δ|/b)(1−z)atanh(tz). For every 0<t<1, its second derivative is −2t(1−t²z)/(1−t²z²)²<0, forcing a unique interior maximum; at t=0 entropy vanishes identically. The critical-point equation and implicit derivative give 1/2<z*(t)<s, monotone z*, with atanh(s)=1/(1+s), and the sharp bound (1−s)/s < bκ* <1. Hyperbolic point-reset identities yield κ*(r)=D/L+rL/12+O(r²) at small r and κ*/sqrt(Dr)→(1−s)/(2s) at large r. The joint convexity of Jeffreys divergence and monotone point-source location dependence establish the endpoint-source envelope for arbitrary μ. I independently simplified the F formula, checked the critical root s≈0.564376588560400 and strict optimum shape at multiple contrasts. The analytic proof, not finite tests, covers all asserted parameters.
